movements.name: Czech Avant-garde
movements.summary: Devětsil's Poetism turned Constructivist type, photomontage and the picture poem into a playful, lyrical modernism; Teige and Sutnar made it typography.

principles.name: The picture poem
principles.idea: Image and verse share one surface; the page is a canvas, not a column of text.
principles.example: Karel Teige, typography for Jaroslav Seifert's Na vlnách TSF, 1925

principles.name: Letters as bodies
principles.idea: The alphabet is performed: each letter staged as a pose and a photomontage.

principles.name: Constructivist economy for a lyrical end
principles.idea: Sans-serifs, bars and photographs used for joy and everyday modern life rather than agitation.
principles.example: Karel Teige, covers for ReD (Revue Devětsilu), 1927–1931

principles.name: Type alone holds attention
principles.idea: A strict hierarchy of type sizes replaces the picture.
principles.example: Ladislav Sutnar, Visit the Modern Textile Exhibition poster, 1930

movements.name: Polish Poster School
movements.summary: State-commissioned film, theatre and circus posters where one authored, painterly metaphor and hand-drawn lettering replaced the star portrait and the grid.

principles.name: The poster as authored picture
principles.idea: The designer is also the image-maker; the personal hand is the point, not a house style.
principles.example: Henryk Tomaszewski, Obywatel Kane (Citizen Kane) poster, 1948

principles.name: Metaphor over depiction
principles.idea: One shortcut image stands for the whole film or play; indirection also passed the censor.

principles.name: Hand-lettering as image
principles.idea: Type is drawn, not set, and often carries the whole composition.

principles.name: Painterly gesture in print
principles.idea: Gouache, crayon, collage and photomontage go straight into offset lithography.
principles.example: Waldemar Świerzy, Czerwona Oberża (The Red Inn) poster, 1955

principles.name: Style follows the subject
principles.idea: No enforced style: baroque, art-nouveau line and halftone montage all belong.

movements.name: Czechoslovak Film Poster
movements.summary: State-distributor film posters by architects, painters and typographers, lightly censored for export, mixing avant-garde typography with surrealist painting.

principles.name: Typography as the film's voice
principles.idea: The title is designed rather than illustrated; letterform carries mood.

principles.name: Surrealist painting on the street
principles.idea: Magic-realist painting replaces the publicity still.
principles.example: Josef Vyleťal, Panna a netvor poster, awarded Chicago 1979

principles.name: The painter's catalogue
principles.idea: The poster is one medium within a painter's practice, alongside books and stage design.
principles.example: Karel Vaca, 341 theatre and film posters, 1950s–1980s

movements.name: Saqqakhaneh
movements.summary: Iranian neo-traditional modernism that turned Shi'a votive objects, talismans, locks and script into modern painting, sculpture and graphic form.

principles.name: Folk-devotional objects as modern material
principles.idea: Locks, hands, talismans and astrolabes from water shrines become modern form.
principles.example: Parviz Tanavoli, Heech series, from the 1960s

principles.name: Script as visual matter
principles.idea: Letters are used for rhythm and charge rather than legibility.
principles.example: Hossein Zenderoudi, Who is this Hossein the world is crazy about?, linocut, 1958

principles.name: A grid of signs
principles.idea: Surfaces covered edge to edge with letters and numerals like a talisman.
principles.example: Hossein Zenderoudi, K+L+32+H+4. Mon père et moi, 1962 (MoMA)

keyWorks.title: Who is this Hossein the world is crazy about?

movements.name: Iranian Graphic Design
movements.summary: Persian-script modernism: marks built from letters, Kanoon's illustrated books, festival posters, revolutionary posters, then the script-first cultural poster.

principles.name: The mark built from Persian letters
principles.idea: A logotype grows out of the script's own rhythm rather than a Latin monogram.
principles.example: Morteza Momayez, ISIRI standards mark turning the initials into 'Iran', 1985

principles.name: One concentrated image
principles.idea: The poster states the film in a single image, partly learned from Polish posters.

principles.name: Children's culture as laboratory
principles.idea: At Kanoon, designers worked across picture books, animation and posters.
principles.example: Farshid Mesghali, The Little Black Fish illustrations, 1968

principles.name: Calligraphy as structure
principles.idea: Letters enlarged and interlaced become architecture, not decoration.
principles.example: Mohammad Ehsai and Morteza Momayez, Reza Abbasi Museum mark, 1976

principles.name: Script as the whole image
principles.idea: Hand-built Persian lettering is the poster's image and concept at once.
principles.example: Reza Abedini, Fajr Film Festival best-poster winners, from 1993

keyWorks.title: Mahi-ye siyah-e kuchulu (The Little Black Fish)

movements.name: Hurufiyya
movements.summary: Pan-Arab and Islamic-world movement freeing Arabic calligraphy from classical rules and using letters as abstract signs of post-colonial identity.

principles.name: Free the letter from the rules
principles.idea: Classical proportion and devotional use are broken; the letter is distorted and abstracted.
principles.example: Madiha Omar, 22 calligraphy-based paintings, Georgetown Public Library, Washington, 1949

principles.name: The letter as sign, emptied and refilled
principles.idea: A character keeps its cultural link while losing its linguistic function.
principles.example: Shakir Hassan Al Said, One Dimension Group manifesto, Baghdad, 1971

principles.name: Geometry as a bridge
principles.idea: Kufic and the square link Islamic pattern, icon and architecture.

principles.name: Generations
principles.idea: Nationalist pioneers, then exiles, then a third generation using script purely abstractly.
principles.example: Word into Art: Artists of the Modern Middle East, British Museum, 2006

movements.name: Arabic Modernism
movements.summary: Making Arabic script work with modern machines and media: type reform, Cairo and Beirut book and children's design, bilingual type and research.

principles.name: Simplify for the machine, keep the identity
principles.idea: Reduce contextual forms for print while keeping letters recognisable.
principles.example: Nasri Khattar, Unified Arabic, patented 1947, launched 1957

principles.name: The book cover as public art
principles.idea: A single illustrator's hand across thousands of covers becomes a shared visual language.
principles.example: Helmi El Touni, more than 3,000 book covers for Cairo and Beirut publishers

principles.name: Children's design as cultural sovereignty
principles.idea: Arab children's books written and drawn in the region, not translated.
principles.example: Mohieddine Ellabbad, Dar al-Fata al-Arabi, founded 1974

principles.name: Bilingual parity
principles.idea: Arabic and Latin designed together as equals, not Arabic retrofitted.

principles.name: Research as design
principles.idea: Writing the script's design history is part of the practice.
principles.example: Huda Smitshuijzen AbiFarès, Arabic Typography: A Comprehensive Sourcebook, 2001

keyWorks.title: International Year of the Child poster (UNICEF)

figures.name: Karel Teige
figures.summary: Leader and theorist of Devětsil and Poetism whose book typography and photomontage made the Czech avant-garde a typographic movement.

principles.name: Typography as poetry's second voice
principles.idea: The layout carries the poem's meaning, not just its text.

principles.name: Montage over illustration
principles.idea: Photographs are cut and recombined into a new statement.

principles.name: Function as a social programme
principles.idea: Design as the scientific solution of exact tasks of rational construction.

figures.name: Ladislav Sutnar
figures.role: Graphic, exhibition and information designer, educator
figures.summary: Prague avant-garde typographer who, after emigrating in 1939, founded American information design at Sweet's Catalog Service.

principles.name: Controlled visual flow
principles.idea: Colour, shape and size direct the eye through dense information.

principles.name: Punctuation as navigation
principles.idea: Brackets, tabs, numerals and arrows are wayfinding tools.
principles.example: Parentheses around US telephone area codes, late 1950s

principles.name: Type alone can hold attention
principles.idea: Hierarchy of sizes replaces the picture.

figures.name: Henryk Tomaszewski
figures.summary: Father of the Polish Poster School; five Vienna first prizes in 1948 and head of the Warsaw Academy poster studio, 1952–1985.

principles.name: Strip to the sign
principles.idea: Analyse, discard the superfluous, drop the adjectives, arrive at a shortcut sign.

principles.name: The lettering is the image
principles.idea: His own handwriting increasingly becomes the whole poster.

principles.name: Train the eye, not the hand
principles.idea: Teach through abstract concepts set as riddles to be solved.

figures.name: Józef Mroszczak
figures.summary: Co-founder of Projekt magazine and founder of the Warsaw International Poster Biennale, who professionalised Polish design education.

principles.name: Build the institution
principles.idea: A magazine, a biennale and a museum gave the school its international stage.

principles.name: Balance design and expression
principles.idea: Rigorous composition kept painterly.

principles.name: The poster as public conscience
principles.idea: Posters as moral statements, not only announcements.
principles.example: Auschwitz – Never Again project, prize at the 1966 Biennale

figures.name: Jan Lenica
figures.summary: Poster artist and cut-out animator whose sinuous, multiplied contour revived Art Nouveau line for the 1960s.

principles.name: The contour as a living thing
principles.idea: Flowing multiple outlines carry the image's energy.

principles.name: Poster and animation as one art
principles.idea: Cut-out figures move between street and screen.

principles.name: Absurdity as commentary
principles.idea: Bureaucracy and the machine swallow the individual.

figures.name: Roman Cieślewicz
figures.summary: Polish School photomontagist who moved to Paris in 1963, art-directed Elle and made the halftone dot and mirror image expressive.

principles.name: Maximum picture, maximum information
principles.idea: The poster is the street picture and must hit as hard as possible.

principles.name: Mechanise the image
principles.idea: Enlarged halftone, mirroring and repetition make the image pulse.

principles.name: Montage from the archive
principles.idea: Old masters and press photographs collide into new meaning.

figures.name: Waldemar Świerzy
figures.summary: Prolific Polish School portraitist, with more than 1,500 posters, who brought gestural painting, pop-art and folk art into the poster.

principles.name: Bring painting into the poster
principles.idea: Gesture, lyrical abstraction and pop-art go straight onto the sheet.
principles.example: Hej kolęda poster for No To Co, 1968

principles.name: The portrait as sign
principles.idea: A few traits plus a metaphor for the profession.

principles.name: Legible only at a distance
principles.idea: Up close a mesh of squiggles and dots; from afar a face.

figures.name: Franciszek Starowieyski
figures.summary: Baroque-surrealist of the Polish School: skulls, anatomy and mock-17th-century calligraphy turned the poster into an autonomous artwork.

principles.name: The baroque as resistance
principles.idea: Morbid, ornamental imagery against both Socialist Realism and cheerful circus posters.

principles.name: The poster as autonomous work
principles.idea: Posters as 'Franciszek Starowieyski presents', not as advertisements.

principles.name: Persona as method
principles.idea: From 1970 he back-dated his works by 300 years.

keyWorks.title: Płaczący gołąbek pokoju (The Crying Dove of Peace)

figures.name: Wiktor Górka
figures.summary: Polish School film-poster master of the fused emblem, best known for Cabaret, who carried the method to Cuba and Mexico.

principles.name: The composite emblem
principles.idea: Two motifs fuse into a third, damning meaning.
principles.example: Kabaret: dancers' legs and Joel Grey's face form a swastika, 1973

principles.name: Teaching as export
principles.idea: The school's method carried abroad through workshops and teaching.
principles.example: Design workshops in Havana, 1970; teaching in Mexico to the mid-1990s

figures.name: Zdeněk Ziegler
figures.summary: Architect-trained typographer of the Czechoslovak New Wave film poster, later book designer, stamp designer and rector of VŠUP Prague.

principles.name: Type chosen for the text's nature
principles.idea: Every typeface decision follows the character of the text.
principles.example: Book series for Odeon and Československý spisovatel, from 1963

principles.name: One designer, one whole
principles.idea: Poster, book series, identity and stamp form one designed world.

figures.name: Parviz Tanavoli
figures.summary: Key Saqqakhaneh artist whose Heech sculptures cast the Persian word 'nothing' as a solid character.

principles.name: A word as an object
principles.idea: Three nasta'liq letters cast as a figure that sits, is caged or embraced.

principles.name: The craftsman's archive
principles.idea: Locks, rugs and salt bags studied as design sources.

principles.name: Nothingness as content
principles.idea: Sufi creation from nothing, made tangible.

figures.name: Morteza Momayez
figures.summary: Father of modern Iranian graphic design: Persian-letter marks, Tehran Film Festival art direction, and founder of the profession's schools and societies.

principles.name: A mark from the letters' own rhythm
principles.idea: Initials in Persian script generate the monogram.
principles.example: Iranian Association of Certified Accountants mark, 1974

principles.name: Derive the symbol from local form
principles.idea: City gates become a flower; Maragheh brickwork becomes a car marque.

principles.name: The designer builds the profession
principles.idea: Atelier, syndicate, biennials, society and magazine.
principles.example: Iranian Graphic Designers Society, founding president, 1997

figures.name: Ghobad Shiva
figures.summary: Founder of the graphics departments at Iranian national broadcasting and Soroush, co-founder of IGDS and planner of the first Tehran poster biennial.

principles.name: Iranian themes in a graphic idiom
principles.idea: Persian motifs restated as flat poster shapes.

principles.name: Design departments as infrastructure
principles.idea: In-house studios at broadcasters and publishers as public design.
principles.example: Graphics department of Iranian radio and television, 1968

figures.name: Farshid Mesghali
figures.summary: Kanoon illustrator, animator and poster designer; the only Iranian Hans Christian Andersen Award winner (1974).

principles.name: Cross every medium
principles.idea: The same designer makes the book, the film and the poster.
principles.example: The Little Black Fish, 1968; Look Again, 1974

principles.name: Technique follows the story
principles.idea: Lithography, collage, watercolour or lithographed-book style as each story needs.

principles.name: One clear image for an auteur's film
principles.idea: The poster distils the film into a single image.

keyWorks.title: Mahi-ye siyah-e kuchulu (The Little Black Fish)

figures.name: Mohammad Ehsai
figures.summary: Pioneer of Iranian calligraphic painting (naqqashi-khatt) who enlarged and interlaced letters into monumental abstract structures.

principles.name: Enlarge until meaning yields to rhythm
principles.idea: Letters repeated and interlaced become architecture.

principles.name: Mastery first, then rupture
principles.idea: Full classical training underwrites the modern break.
principles.example: Calligraphy for the Reza Abbasi Museum mark, 1976

figures.name: Reza Abedini
figures.summary: Leading post-1990s Iranian poster designer whose Persian lettering is both image and concept; 2006 Prince Claus Award laureate.

principles.name: The letter as aesthetic and concept
principles.idea: Persian script carries the idea, not just the caption.

principles.name: Reread the heritage, don't quote it
principles.idea: Rodchenko, Ikko Tanaka and Cieślewicz alongside Qajar painters.
principles.example: Gold medal, 8th International Poster Biennial, Mexico, 2004

principles.name: Dissolve design into art
principles.idea: Posters that double as typographic artworks.

keyWorks.title: Fajr International Film Festival best film poster
8th International Poster Biennial, Mexico, gold medal

figures.name: Madiha Omar
figures.summary: Iraqi painter, generally seen as the first modern artist to build abstract paintings from Arabic letters (Washington, 1949).

principles.name: The letter as abstract element
principles.idea: Calligraphy as inspiration for abstract form, not as text.
principles.example: Arabic Calligraphy: An Element of Inspiration in Abstract Art, 1949

principles.name: Secular use of a sacred script
principles.idea: Arabic letters in secular modern painting.
principles.example: 48 paintings at the Ibn Sina exhibition, Baghdad, 1952

keyWorks.title: Arabic Calligraphy: An Element of Inspiration in Abstract Art

figures.name: Kamal Boullata
figures.summary: Palestinian artist-historian whose Kufic-on-the-square silkscreens bridged icon and Islamic geometry; author of the standard history of Palestinian art.

principles.name: The square as root
principles.idea: Two intersecting squares in a circle unite star, mandorla and Jerusalem's sacred plans.

principles.name: Write the image
principles.idea: From icon painting: the iconographer writes rather than paints.

principles.name: Stencil precision
principles.idea: Pochoir and silkscreen give crisp, measured flat colour.

keyWorks.title: Palestinian Art: From 1850 to the Present

figures.name: Nasri Khattar
figures.summary: Lebanese architect who devised Unified Arabic, a one-form-per-letter printing script of 33 glyphs (patented 1947, launched 1957).

principles.name: Rationalise the system, not the letter
principles.idea: Combine isolated and connected features so each letter needs one form.

principles.name: For print only
principles.idea: Handwriting stays; the reform is for the machine.

figures.name: Mohieddine Ellabbad
figures.summary: Egyptian illustrator-designer who built a modern Arab children's book culture through Dar al-Fata al-Arabi and books about images.

principles.name: Visual literacy for the reader
principles.idea: Books about images, written and designed by the designer.

principles.name: Memory as material
principles.idea: Visual memories addressed across generations.

principles.name: Arab publishing for Arab children
principles.idea: Build the publisher, not only the pages.

figures.name: Helmi El Touni
figures.role: Painter, book and magazine designer, illustrator
figures.summary: Egyptian painter-designer of more than 3,000 book covers across Cairo and Beirut, setting popular imagery in a flat modern frame.

principles.name: Popular imagery, modern frame
principles.idea: Folk and popular-print motifs restated in flat poster colour.
principles.example: UNICEF International Year of the Child poster, 1979

principles.name: The cover as a repeated public gallery
principles.idea: Volume makes one hand a shared visual language.

keyWorks.title: International Year of the Child poster (UNICEF)

figures.name: Huda Smitshuijzen AbiFarès
figures.summary: Author of Arabic Typography (2001) and founder of the Khatt Foundation (2004), the research and matchmaking hub of bilingual Arabic type.

principles.name: Structure before style
principles.idea: Analyse Arabic typography structurally and theoretically.

principles.name: Matchmaking
principles.idea: Pair Arabic and Latin designers to make genuinely bilingual families.

principles.name: Build the library
principles.idea: Publish the region's design history.

events.label: Devětsil founded in Prague
events.note: The Czech avant-garde union that produced Poetism, the picture poem and Teige's typography.

events.label: Abeceda published
events.note: Nezval, Teige and Mayerová stage the alphabet as dance and photomontage, a landmark of avant-garde book typography.

events.label: Teige lectures at the Bauhaus
events.note: Prague's leading theorist teaches in Dessau, linking Czech Poetism to the Bauhaus.

events.label: Sutnar stays in New York
events.note: After the Nazi occupation the Czech avant-garde typographer remains in the US and goes on to found American information design.

events.label: Unified Arabic patented
events.note: Nasri Khattar's one-form-per-letter Arabic print script cuts the glyph set to 33 for machine typesetting.

events.label: Polish posters win in Vienna
events.note: Tomaszewski's five first prizes start international attention to the Polish poster.

events.label: Madiha Omar's calligraphic paintings shown in Washington
events.note: Generally taken as the first exhibition of modern art built from Arabic letters, the start of hurufiyya.

events.label: Sindbad magazine launched in Cairo
events.note: Hussein Bicar's Sindbad, Egypt's first children's magazine, trained a generation of Arab illustrators.

events.label: Projekt magazine founded in Warsaw
events.note: The design magazine of the Polish thaw, co-designed by Cieślewicz, carried the school abroad.

events.label: Kanoon founded in Tehran
events.note: The children's institute became the laboratory of Iranian illustration, animation and graphic design.

events.label: First International Poster Biennale, Warsaw
events.note: The world's first recurring event devoted to the poster.

events.label: First Shiraz Arts Festival
events.note: An annual international festival (1967–1977) whose posters and programmes were key commissions for Iranian designers.

events.label: Poster Museum at Wilanów opens
events.note: The world's first museum dedicated to the poster.

events.label: Polish poster designers teach in Havana
events.note: Górka and Świerzy lead workshops in Cuba, linking the Polish and Cuban poster schools.

events.label: One Dimension Group manifesto
events.note: Shakir Hassan Al Said's Baghdad manifesto gives hurufiyya its most articulate theory.

events.label: Dar al-Fata al-Arabi founded
events.note: A Beirut-based Arab children's publisher, co-founded by Ellabbad, that built a regional visual culture for young readers.

events.label: Tehran Museum of Contemporary Art opens
events.note: Kamran Diba's museum showed Iranian modernists beside a major Western collection, two years before the revolution.

events.label: Iranian Revolution
events.note: Ends royal cultural patronage and makes the political and martyrdom poster Iran's dominant public genre.

events.label: Communist rule ends in Poland and Czechoslovakia
events.note: The market economy removes the state commissioning system that sustained the Polish and Czech poster schools.

events.label: Iranian Graphic Designers Society founded
events.note: Momayez's professional society rebuilds Iranian design's institutions after the revolution.

events.label: AbiFarès publishes Arabic Typography
events.note: The first comprehensive modern sourcebook on Arabic type, written because none existed to teach from.

events.label: Khatt Foundation founded
events.note: An Amsterdam foundation that became the hub for bilingual Arabic–Latin type design and research.

events.label: Unified Arabic revived digitally
events.note: The 29LT foundry turns Khattar's 1947 reform into working digital fonts.
